title: A bounded strict tower with epimorphic top transitions has a bounded derived limit
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site. Let $(P_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a strict inverse tower of integer cochain complexes of $\mathcal R$-module sheaves, with chain maps $t_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-inverse-system]. Write $Q$ for localization into $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R))$ and $H^j$ for its cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L$ be any derived limit of the tower $(Q(P_n),Q(t_n))_{n\geq1}$, in the sense that it occurs in a Roos distinguished triangle
$$L\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}Q(P_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_{n\geq1}Q(P_n)\longrightarrow L[1],\qquad \operatorname{pr}_n s=Q(t_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$$
[def-weil-derived-limit]. Suppose $a\leq b$ are integers, $H^j(P_n)=0$ for every $n\geq1$ and every $j\notin[a,b]$, and each $H^b(t_n):H^b(P_{n+1})\to H^b(P_n)$ is an epimorphism. Then $H^j(L)=0$ for every $j\notin[a,b]$. Only epimorphy on the top cohomology sheaves is required, not degreewise epimorphy of the strict tower maps.

source.place: Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, (5)-(7) and proof: termwise product model, Roos triangle identification, Milnor exact sequence, and vanishing of the first derived limit for an epimorphic tower, on the small pro-etale site.

proof.text: Put $A_n=Q(P_n)$ and let $B$ be the product used in the given Roos triangle. By [det-pe-products-derived], the termwise product complex $C=\prod_nP_n$ represents a product of the $A_n$, and its cohomology comparison is $H^j(C)\cong V_j:=\prod_nH^j(P_n)$. By [def-weil-category-product], the maps from $B$ to $Q(C)$ and back induced by the two sets of projections are inverse: each composite has the original projections, hence is the identity. The resulting comparison $c_j:H^j(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_j$ therefore has components $H^j(\operatorname{pr}_n)$. Let $S:C\to C$ be the chain map with $n$th coordinate $t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Comparing projections shows that $s$ corresponds to $Q(S)$, and $1-s$ corresponds to $Q(1-S)$. On cohomology, [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] computes $H^j(1-S)$ on cycles modulo boundaries: it sends $[x]$ to $[x]-[Sx]$. Thus $c_jH^j(1-s)c_j^{-1}=d_j:=1-T_j$, where the $n$th coordinate of $T_j$ is $H^j(t_n)$ after the $(n+1)$st projection. This identifies both the objects and the actual endomorphism for the supplied product.

Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the distinguished Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit] supplied with $L$. With the product comparisons of Step 1, its exact sequence contains, for every integer $j$,
$$V_{j-1}\xrightarrow{d_{j-1}}V_{j-1}\xrightarrow{\delta_j}H^j(L)\longrightarrow V_j\xrightarrow{d_j}V_j.$$
Here the connecting morphism has been composed with the inverse product comparison on its source. Exactness is unchanged by these isomorphisms. This is the product form of the Milnor calculation in Tag 0947, applied directly to the given triangle; no assertion of canonical uniqueness for triangulated cones is needed.

If $j<a$, then both $j-1$ and $j$ are below $a$. If $j>b+1$, both are above $b$. In either case every factor of $V_{j-1}$ and $V_j$ is zero by hypothesis. A product of zero objects is zero: every family of maps into its factors consists of zero maps, so its identity is zero by uniqueness of a product map. The sequence of Step 2 consequently has $0\to H^j(L)\to0$ exact at its middle term, forcing $H^j(L)=0$.

Apply the first assertion of [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] to the tower $M_n=H^b(P_n)$ of $\mathcal R$-module sheaves, with transitions $H^b(t_n)$. Its site and ring sheaf are exactly the ones fixed in the statement, and its epimorphy hypothesis is precisely the top-transition assumption. The change from indices $n\geq1$ here to $n\geq0$ there is the order isomorphism $n\mapsto n+1$, which leaves the product coordinates and consecutive transitions unchanged. The conclusion is that $d_b=1-T_b:V_b\to V_b$ is an epimorphism. This uses no epimorphy on the terms of the complexes or in other cohomological degrees.

source.place: first assertion: one minus transition on the product is an epimorphism

proof.text: It remains to consider $j=b+1$. The bound on each $P_n$ gives $V_{b+1}=0$. In Step 2 the composite $\delta_{b+1}d_b$ is zero, and $d_b$ is epic by Step 4; canceling this epimorphism gives $\delta_{b+1}=0$. Exactness at $H^{b+1}(L)$, whose next object is zero, also says that the image of $\delta_{b+1}$ is all of $H^{b+1}(L)$. Its image is zero, hence $H^{b+1}(L)=0$. Together with Step 3 this proves the required vanishing for every $j\notin[a,b]$.
